transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-25
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Sarah Kim (Emerald VP Eng), Dr. Nikhil Rao (Emerald Head ML Infra), Lisa Park (Emerald Security), Carlos Mendes (Emerald SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Followup on incident on 2026-09-18 where inference throughput dropped and 95/99th latencies spiked. Talked root cause: cache eviction after model roll, autoscaler thrash, fallback to larger model, and DB throttling on metrics collectors. Agreed on next steps: share postmortem deck, run dedicated pilot with KV cache pinning and adjusted autoscaling, share security artifacts.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: all right hey everyone thanks for joining uh this is Jordan from Redwood Lee on the ae team um we have Priya our se and Mateo on the call too hey thanks for making time
00:12 Sarah: yeah thanks Jordan appreciate it we've got kind of a packed agenda we want to make sure we close the loop on the outage and the mitigations, and figure next steps for the pilot
00:22 Priya: cool, quick note I threw the incident timeline slide into the deck, i'll share a link after; redwood dedicated was mis-typed in the auto notes as red wood dedicated so if you see that ignore it
00:34 Carlos: perfect can you also share the logs for the model swap window, that would help our postmortem on our side
00:42 Jordan: yep we'll redact pii and send, expect a link by monday, um question are we looking for raw traces or a trimmed bundle?
00:51 Carlos: trimmed bundle is fine, and if you can include the autoscaler events that happened around 14:12 that would be great
01:05 Nikhil: just to summarize from our side, we saw a sudden increase in tail latency starting ~14:10, traffic didn't change much but the model variant swap and kv cache miss rate spiked; do we have a theory for why the kv cache got evicted?
01:22 Priya: what we're seeing in the runtime traces is a combination of a model variant rollout that didn't warm the KV cache and then an aggressive scale-down that removed hot workers; there was also an unexpected fallback to larger fp16 model on a subset of requests which increased per-token latency
01:38 Lisa: and that triggered a cascade because a bunch of our downstream consumers retried which pushed up qps, yeah we saw retries on the client side
01:48 Jordan: right so root cause we think is threefold: rollout without cache prewarm, autoscaler policy didn't respect ongoing warm-up windows, and fallback model selection criteria was too lenient under degraded capacity
02:02 Sarah: okay that aligns with what we saw; the thing we're most worried about is this happening in production again during a peak window 1 what are short term mitigations?
02:13 Priya: short term we reverted the rollout and pinned the older variant, increased min replicas for the pool for the next 48 hours, and added a rule to avoid fallback to larger model variants if current latency above threshold; this was implemented as a hotfix at 14:28 and restored normal 95th/99th within about 7 minutes
02:34 Nikhil: okay can you confirm the hotfix involved changing the autoscaler cooldown and minReplica params? our metrics show replica count went from 8 to 2 which is when cache miss rate skyrocketed
02:45 Priya: yes exactly, we bumped minReplicas from 2 to 6 and increased the cooldown from 30s to 3m, that stopped the thrash; we'll send the exact config diff in the deck
02:57 Mateo: and from CS side we also opened a support priority ticket and set up the incident bridge for your team, we left notes for your oncall so hopefully the handoff was smooth
03:10 Sarah: thanks mateo that was helpful 
03:16 Carlos: any long term reliability changes you're proposing? we'd like to avoid quantity band-aids
03:22 Priya: long term we're proposing three changes: 1) prewarm cache for rollouts using a canary warm-up phase, 2) improved autoscaler logic that factors in KV cache hotness and in-flight requests when scaling down, and 3) stricter model fallback rules and better binary compatibility checks so a fallback doesn't pick a larger variant unexpectedly
03:44 Nikhil: the autoscaler one is key for us; can you give any details on how you'd quantify 'kv cache hotness'? we need something we can adopt in our SLOs
03:54 Priya: sure, rough idea is percent of requests hitting KV cache within a moving window and average per-request cold-start token penalty; we can provide a metric name and suggested threshold e.g. kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.85 for 2m window triggers holdoff on scale down
04:12 Lisa: from security/compliance perspective we need to see the audit logs for the rollback and any admin actions. Also need confirmation that none of the PII persisted in any debug dumps
04:25 Jordan: understood we'll include an audit export and a statement about debug dumps 1 our engineers confirmed no PII was written to logs, but we'll include redaction notes and samples for review
04:36 Sarah: also we need the timeline of who approved the rollback, the ticket IDs and the contact for the engineer who made the change
04:44 Jordan: yep adding that to the deck, will include timestamps and the bridge recording link
04:50 Carlos: small pedantic note 1 in the initial auto notes your system wrote KV as k v which made searching hard, lol
04:57 Jordan: noted, sorry about that
05:02 Nikhil: on the pilot vs hosted decision 1 if we do a dedicated pilot what capacity guarantees do we get? and can we replicate the traffic pattern that caused the incident?
05:14 Priya: for a dedicated pilot we can provision an isolated GPU pool with pinned KV cache parameters, configurable autoscaling policies and a guaranteed throughput floor; we'll run your traffic replay for the bench and aim for 99th latency SLOs you specify
05:29 Sarah: what's the expected cost delta for dedicated vs hosted for a 4-week pilot? we need numbers to budget
05:36 Jordan: i'll put a ballpark in the follow-up email 1 but expect dedicated to be higher due to reserved capacity; we can show cost/perf tradeoffs in the bench report so you can see unit economics at your observed qps
05:49 Lisa: and for security packages 1 we need KMS integration and HSM options, plus the right to rotate keys on schedule; is that supported for dedicated/private?
05:58 Mateo: yes KMS is supported for dedicated and private, HSM integrations are available for private deployments; we'll share the integration guide and our key rotation policies in the doc pack
06:10 Sarah: will there be any compliance documentation update after the pilot? we require an attestation for HIPAA controls if we handle ePHI during the pilot
06:20 Jordan: we'll include HIPAA scoping notes; we have customers running PHI workloads on private and dedicated and can share standard attestation language, Mateo will follow up
06:30 Priya: back to the tech, one nuance is the model fallback logic in runtime uses a compatibility tree; in this case the fallback node matched but the performance profile was inaccurate because quantization settings differed which produced a longer per-token time; we'll tighten that check to include perf estimates at runtime
06:53 Nikhil: did you see any memory pressure or OOMs during the window? our infra logs show some worker restarts
07:02 Priya: we saw elevated RSS on several workers and two evictions; i think the larger variant had higher working set which pushed memory pressure and triggered restarts; we'll add memory headroom checks before failing over
07:18 Carlos: okay that makes sense, please add a memory+latency guard to the fallback decision table
07:27 Priya: noted
07:31 Sarah: can we talk about observability improvements? specifically we want route-level error budgets and token-level cost breakdowns for the route that hit the incident
07:43 Mateo: we can extend retention for the route and add a dashboard with token-level breakdowns and 99/999 latencies; i'll propose a dashboard template and share it in the next 48 hours
07:55 Sarah: nice, also need to know if we can hold a read-only view for our SREs into the console for the pilot
08:03 Jordan: yes we can grant read-only RBAC for the pilot cluster and reduce retainment if needed; we'll include the RBAC roles in the doc pack
08:12 Lisa: about encryption at rest 1 can you confirm all intermediate cache artifacts are encrypted and keys are customer-managed in the dedicated pilot?
08:22 Priya: yes, cache snapshots and any persisted artifacts can be encrypted using your KMS and we can enable customer-managed keys for the pilot pool
08:33 Sarah: great, that addresses a lot of compliance concerns; next question from our legal: what does rollback of model variants look like in terms of audit trail?
08:44 Jordan: we keep an immutable audit trail for deploys and rollbacks including user id, commit hash, timestamps; we'll include the sample audit extract for the incident
08:55 Carlos: will the bench include a simulated spike with retries? because the retry storms definitely amplified things for us
09:05 Priya: yes we can replay your traffic trace including client retries and we can also run a synthetic spike test to exercise autoscaler and cache warm-up behavior
09:18 Nikhil: regarding SLOs, if we set a 99th token latency SLO, what are the suggested guardrails to prevent degradation during rollout?
09:29 Priya: suggested guardrails: require canary warm-up to reach 0.95 kv hit ratio before promoting, block scale-down for 2m after any variant promotion, and add a soft limit to disallow fallback to larger variants unless CPU/memory headroom>25%
09:45 Sarah: sounds reasonable, please codify those into the SLO doc so we can take it back to upper management
09:53 Jordan: will do, we'll include a recommended SLO/guardrail doc in the follow-up
10:01 Carlos: timeline wise what's realistic for the dedicated pilot? i know you mentioned 4 weeks but can we start earlier?
10:10 Priya: if we get approvals and sample traffic by end of week we can stand up the pilot cluster in ~7 business days, so start in mid-october is realistic; bench and initial report in two weeks after start
10:24 Sarah: okay timeline noted, we'll aim to confirm by next week
10:30 Mateo: just to recap actions: we'll share the postmortem deck, perf logs, SOC2/HIPAA artifacts, KMS/HSM integration guide, and pilot proposal; Jordan will include cost estimate; Priya will set up bench plan; Emerald to provide traffic trace and peak windows
10:47 Jordan: quick undocumented thing 1 there was a small typo in the incident notes where 'kv cache' was transcribed as 'k v cache' which made the automated anomaly detection miss the signal, we're correcting that in the pipeline too
11:00 Lisa: thanks that's important for our analytics, good catch
11:07 Sarah: any other questions from the team?
11:12 Carlos: one last ask, can you include an example of the autoscaler config diff so our infra team can review?
11:20 Priya: absolutely, we'll include the exact config diff and also a suggested conservative autoscaler policy for your workload
11:29 Nikhil: and please include the bench code repo or a reproducible harness so we can run locally against our staging data
11:37 Priya: yes we'll share the harness repo link with instructions
11:42 Jordan: cool, if no more questions we'll wrap; thanks everyone for the thorough discussion, we'll follow up with notes and artifacts
11:50 Sarah: thanks all appreciate it
11:53 Jordan: bye everyone
52:00 [meeting ends]

References/attachments mentioned: link to postmortem deck (to be sent), perf logs bundle (trimmed), SOC2 and HIPAA checklist, KMS/HSM integration guide, pilot proposal, bench harness repo link
